concepts.def: How speakers swap floor in conversation
Linked pair — question + answer, greet + greet
Two speakers talking at the same time
Cutting in BEFORE the speaker finishes
Jumping in instantly, no gap, no overlap

walkthroughs.body_html: In smooth talk, turns swap with tiny gaps. Speakers cue 'I'm done' with falling tone or eye contact.

Some turns DEMAND a partner: 'Hi' → 'Hi.' 'How are you?' → 'Fine, thanks.'

If the second part is missing, things feel weird.

'Mm.' 'Right.' 'Yeah.' 'Wow.'

These aren't interruptions — they're supportive signals that say 'keep going'.

options: Back-channelling
Adjacency pair
Overlap
Filler

mcqs.q: What is the difference between descriptive and prescriptive approaches to language?
options: Descriptivists describe how language is actually used; prescriptivists rule on how language ought to be used — modern linguistics is descriptivist.
Both terms mean the same — analysing language scientifically.
Descriptivists describe written language and prescriptivists describe spoken language.
Register is the same as accent.
Register is just how loud you speak.
Register is the same as accent.
A variety of language used in a particular social setting — varying by formality, field (topic) and mode (spoken/written) to suit audience and purpose.
Convergence means two languages merge into one new language.

mcqs.q: What is convergence in accommodation theory?
options: Convergence is when two speakers start using identical accents permanently.
Register is the same as accent.
Convergence means two languages merge into one new language.
When a speaker adjusts their speech to be more similar to their interlocutor's — to express solidarity, gain approval or ease communication.
